blocks.text: Kursimizdagi barcha gaplar Britaniya inglizchasida (British English): colour, flat, at the weekend, I've got. Lekin filmlar, seriallar, YouTube, dasturlash va xalqaro biznesda ko'pincha Amerika inglizchasini (American English) eshitasiz. Ikkalasi ham to'liq to'g'ri, standart til — biri ikkinchisidan «yaxshiroq» emas. Farqlar katta emas: grammatikada bir nechta, imloda bir necha qolip, eng ko'pi esa **lug'atda**. Maqsad — ikkalasini ham tushunish, o'zingiz yozganda esa bittasini tanlab, **izchil** ishlatish.
Belgilar: misollarda **(UK)** — Britaniya varianti, **(US)** — Amerika varianti. Lug'at va imlo gaplarida Britaniya so'zidan keyin qavs ichida Amerika muqobili beriladi: lift (US: elevator).

rows: I just **ate**. **Did** you **finish** yet? (Present Perfect ham to'g'ri)
**Have** you **got** a car? I**'ve got to** go.
**Do** you **have** a car? I **have to** go.
It's **gotten** much worse. (have got = «bor» — ikkalasida got)
I suggest that he **should go** / he **goes**.

blocks.text: Diqqat: **03/04/2026** Britaniyada — 3-aprel, Amerikada — 4-mart. Chipta, viza, shartnoma va imtihon sanasini yozganda chalkashmaslik uchun oy nomini so'z bilan yozing: 3 April 2026.
Eng xavflisi — ikkala variantda ham bor, lekin har xil ma'noli so'zlar. Ular kulgili yoki noqulay vaziyatga olib kelishi mumkin:

My **pants** are too long — I need to get them shortened. (US)
Don't get **mad** at me — it wasn't my fault! (US)

blocks.text: O'zbeklarning tipik xatolari: bitta matnda ikki variantni aralashtirish — «My favourite color is grey», «I traveled to the theatre» → bittasini tanlang: favourite **colour** ... grey (UK) yoki favorite **color** ... gray (US); Londonda «Can I have the check?» — tushunishadi, lekin u yerda **the bill**; «I live on the first floor» deb ko'cha sathidagi qavatni nazarda tutish — Britaniyada bu **ground floor**; Britaniyada shim haqida «pants» deyish — **trousers**; «The team is» ni xato deb o'ylash — ikkala variantda ham to'g'ri, Britaniyada esa **are** ham mumkin.

Qoida bitta: **izchillik**. IELTS va boshqa xalqaro imtihonlar ikkala variantni ham qabul qiladi, lekin bitta inshoda aralashtirmang. Bu kursda Britaniya variantini o'rganyapsiz — yozganda shuni tanlang, film va seriallardan Amerika variantini esa tushunish uchun o'rganing. Lug'atlarda **UK** / **US** belgilariga qarang; kompyuter yoki telefonda imlo tekshiruvini «English (UK)» ga qo'ying.

Bog'liq darslar: → 13–14 (Present Perfect va Past Simple), 17 (have va have got), 21 (shall), 32 (needn't), 34 (suggest that ... should), 79 (the team are / is), 121 (at the weekend); noto'g'ri fe'llarning ikki xil shakli → 146-dars; Britaniya imlosi qoidalari → 151-dars.

examples.title: **I've just eaten** (UK) and **I just ate** (US)
examples.description: just, already, yet bilan Britaniyada Present Perfect, Amerikada ko'pincha Past Simple. Juft gaplar: (UK) — Britaniya, (US) — Amerika varianti; ma'nosi bir xil.

sentences.text: **Have** you **finished** the report yet? The boss wants it by noon. (UK)
**Did** you **finish** the report yet? The boss wants it by noon. (US)
I**'ve** just **spoken** to Dilnoza, and she's on her way. (UK)
I just **spoke** to Dilnoza, and she's on her way. (US)
We**'ve** already **seen** that film, so let's choose another one. (UK)
We already **saw** that movie, so let's pick another one. (US)
**Has** the parcel **arrived** yet, or should I call the courier? (UK)
**Did** the package **arrive** yet, or should I call the courier? (US)
Oh no, I**'ve lost** my wallet! **Have** you **seen** it anywhere? (UK)
Oh no, I **lost** my wallet! **Did** you **see** it anywhere? (US)

examples.title: **Have you got** / **Do you have**, **got** / **gotten**
examples.description: Britaniyada have got, shall, needn't ko'p ishlatiladi; Amerikada — do you have, should, don't need to; get ning V3 shakli Amerikada ko'pincha gotten. Juft gaplar: (UK) va (US).

sentences.text: **Have** you **got** any brothers or sisters? (UK)
**Do** you **have** any brothers or sisters? (US)
**Shall** I **book** a table for eight o'clock? (UK)
**Should** I **book** a table for eight o'clock? (US)
Your English **has got** much better since last summer. (UK)
sentences.translation: O'tgan yozdan beri ingliz tilingiz ancha **yaxshilandi**. (Britaniya)

sentences.text: Your English **has gotten** much better since last summer. (US)
sentences.translation: O'tgan yozdan beri ingliz tilingiz ancha **yaxshilandi**. (Amerika)

sentences.text: You **needn't** bring anything — we**'ve got** plenty of food. (UK)
sentences.translation: Hech narsa olib kelishingiz **shart emas** — ovqatimiz **ko'p**. (Britaniya)

sentences.text: You **don't need to** bring anything — we **have** plenty of food. (US)
sentences.translation: Hech narsa olib kelishingiz **shart emas** — ovqatimiz **ko'p**. (Amerika)

sentences.text: Sorry, I**'ve got to** go — my taxi's waiting outside. (UK)
Sorry, I **have to** go — my cab's waiting outside. (US)

examples.title: **at the weekend** / **on the weekend** and other pairs
examples.description: Predlog va jamoa otlari bilan farqlar: at / on the weekend, Monday to / through Friday, write to me / write me, in hospital / in the hospital, the team are / is. Juft gaplar: (UK) va (US).

sentences.text: What are you doing **at the weekend**? (UK)
What are you doing **on the weekend**? (US)
The office is open **Monday to Friday**, from nine till six. (UK)
sentences.translation: Ofis **dushanbadan jumagacha**, soat to'qqizdan oltigacha ochiq. (Britaniya)

sentences.text: The office is open **Monday through Friday**, from nine to six. (US)
sentences.translation: Ofis **dushanbadan jumagacha**, soat to'qqizdan oltigacha ochiq. (Amerika)

sentences.text: Don't forget to **write to** me when you get to Seoul! (UK)
Don't forget to **write** me when you get to Seoul! (US)
My grandfather is **in hospital** after a minor operation. (UK)
My grandfather is **in the hospital** after a minor operation. (US)
Our team **are** celebrating their victory in the changing room. (UK)
Our team **is** celebrating its victory in the locker room. (US)

examples.title: Home and town: **flat** (US **apartment**), **lift** (US **elevator**)
examples.description: Uy va shahar so'zlari. Gaplar Britaniya inglizchasida, Amerika muqobili qavs ichida (US: ...) yoki gapning o'zida ko'rsatilgan.

sentences.text: Kamila rents a small **flat** in London, and her friend in Boston lives in an **apartment** of the same size.
sentences.translation: Kamila Londonda kichkina **kvartira** ijaraga oladi, Bostondagi dugonasi ham xuddi shunday **kvartirada** yashaydi.

sentences.text: The **lift** (US: **elevator**) in our building has been broken for a week.
In Britain the **ground floor** is at street level, while Americans call it the **first floor**.
sentences.translation: Britaniyada ko'cha sathidagi qavat **ground floor**, amerikaliklar esa uni **first floor** deyishadi.

sentences.text: Could you take the **rubbish** (US: **garbage**) out before you go to work?
sentences.translation: Ishga ketishdan oldin **axlatni** chiqarib tashlay olasanmi?

sentences.text: The kids are playing in the **garden**, which Americans would call the **yard**.
What's your **postcode**? — In America it's called a **zip code**.
sentences.translation: Pochta **indeksingiz** qanday? — Amerikada u «zip code» deyiladi.

sentences.text: There's a huge **car park** (US: **parking lot**) behind the shopping centre.
Walk on the **pavement** (US: **sidewalk**), not in the road!
The **tap** (US: **faucet**) in the kitchen is dripping again.
Is there a **postbox** (US: **mailbox**) near here? I need to send this letter.
sentences.translation: Yaqin atrofda **pochta qutisi** bormi? Shu xatni jo'natishim kerak.

examples.title: Travel, shops and food: **queue** (US **line**), **bill** (US **check**)
examples.description: Transport, xarid va ovqat so'zlari. Gaplar Britaniya inglizchasida, Amerika muqobili qavs ichida (US: ...) yoki gapning o'zida.

sentences.text: We need to stop for **petrol** (US: **gas**) before we get on the **motorway** (US: **highway**).
In London people take the **Underground**, but in New York they take the **subway**.
sentences.translation: Londonda odamlar **metroda** yuradi, Nyu-Yorkda ham **metroda**, faqat uni «subway» deyishadi.

sentences.text: A **return** ticket (US: **round-trip** ticket) to Samarkand costs less than two singles.
sentences.translation: Samarqandga **borish-kelish** chiptasi ikkita bir tomonlama chiptadan arzonroq.

sentences.text: Tourists were **queuing** (US: standing in **line**) outside the Registan at dawn.
sentences.translation: Sayyohlar tong saharda Registon oldida **navbatda turishardi**.

sentences.text: Could we have the **bill** (US: **check**), please? We're in a bit of a hurry.
British **chips** are American **fries**, and American **chips** are British **crisps**.
sentences.translation: Britaniyadagi «chips» — Amerikadagi «fries», ya'ni **kartoshka fri**; Amerikadagi «chips» esa Britaniyadagi «crisps», ya'ni **chips**.

sentences.text: The kids always want **biscuits** (US: **cookies**) and **sweets** (US: **candy**) after school.
sentences.translation: Bolalar maktabdan keyin doim **pechenye** va **konfet** so'rashadi.

sentences.text: Let's get a **takeaway** (US: **takeout**) tonight — I'm too tired to cook.
sentences.translation: Bugun kechqurun **tayyor ovqat** olaylik — pishirishga holim yo'q.

sentences.text: I'm going to the **chemist's** (US: **drugstore**) to get something for my cough.
sentences.translation: Yo'talimga biror narsa olish uchun **dorixonaga** boryapman.

sentences.text: We're going on **holiday** (US: **vacation**) to Turkey next month.

examples.title: Clothes, school and false friends: **trousers** / **pants**
examples.description: Kiyim, maktab va kundalik hayot so'zlari hamda ikki variantda ma'nosi boshqa bo'lgan so'zlar (pants, football). Amerika muqobili qavs ichida (US: ...).

sentences.text: It's freezing, so wear your **jumper** (US: **sweater**) and your warm **trousers** (US: **pants**).
sentences.translation: Qattiq sovuq, shuning uchun **sviteringni** va issiq **shimingni** kiy.

sentences.text: Be careful: in Britain **pants** means underwear, not trousers!
sentences.translation: Ehtiyot bo'ling: Britaniyada «pants» **ichki kiyim** degani, shim emas!

sentences.text: Our son needs new **trainers** (US: **sneakers**) for his PE lessons.
sentences.translation: O'g'limizga jismoniy tarbiya darsi uchun yangi **krossovka** kerak.

sentences.text: The leaves turn gold here in **autumn**, or in the **fall**, as Americans say.
sentences.translation: Bu yerda **kuzda** barglar sarg'ayadi; amerikaliklar kuzni «fall» deyishadi.

sentences.text: Shall we see a **film** (US: **movie**) at the **cinema** tonight?
My daughter got top **marks** in **maths** this term (US: top **grades** in **math**).
sentences.translation: Qizim bu chorakda **matematikadan** eng yuqori **baholarni** oldi.

sentences.text: Send us your **CV** (US: **résumé**) and a short covering letter by Friday.
sentences.translation: Juma kunigacha **rezyumeingiz** va qisqa ilova xatini yuboring.

sentences.text: My **mobile** (US: **cell phone**) died, so I couldn't call you.
sentences.translation: **Telefonim** o'chib qoldi, shuning uchun senga qo'ng'iroq qila olmadim.

sentences.text: In the US, **football** usually means American football, so the world game is called **soccer**.
sentences.translation: AQShda «football» deganda odatda Amerika futboli tushuniladi, shuning uchun oddiy **futbol** «soccer» deyiladi.

sentences.text: When the power went off, we found a **torch** (US: **flashlight**) in the kitchen drawer.

examples.title: Spelling: **colour** (US **color**), **centre** (US **center**)
examples.description: Imlo farqlari: `-our` / `-or`, `-re` / `-er`, `-ise` / `-ize`, `-ll-` / `-l-`, `-mme` / `-m`, `-ence` / `-ense`, `-ogue` / `-og` va alohida so'zlar. Gaplar Britaniya imlosida, Amerika imlosi qavs ichida.

sentences.text: What **colour** (US: **color**) would you like for the bedroom walls?
The new sports **centre** (US: **center**) is opening next to the **theatre** (US: **theater**).
We need someone to **organise** (US: **organize**) the trip to Khiva.
Last year Farhod **travelled** (US: **traveled**) to twelve countries for work.
sentences.translation: O'tgan yili Farhod ish yuzasidan o'n ikki davlatga **sayohat qildi**.

sentences.text: Have you seen the TV **programme** (US: **program**) about the Aral Sea?
Please pay by **cheque** (US: **check**) or bank transfer.
sentences.translation: Iltimos, **chek** yoki bank o'tkazmasi orqali to'lang.

sentences.text: One of the **tyres** (US: **tires**) was flat, so we arrived late.
sentences.translation: **Shinalardan** biri teshilgan edi, shuning uchun kechikib keldik.

sentences.text: The sky was **grey** (US: **gray**) all day, but it didn't rain.
sentences.translation: Kun bo'yi osmon **kulrang** edi, lekin yomg'ir yog'madi.

sentences.text: The minister of **defence** (US: **defense**) visited the border region yesterday.
sentences.translation: **Mudofaa** vaziri kecha chegara hududiga tashrif buyurdi.

sentences.text: You can order everything from the online **catalogue** (US: **catalog**).
sentences.translation: Hamma narsani onlayn **katalogdan** buyurtma qilish mumkin.

examples.title: Dialogue: an American in London
examples.description: Londonlik Emma va Nyu-Yorkdan kelgan Jeyk suhbati: Jeyk amerikacha gapiradi, Emma esa britaniyacha va ular farqlar ustidan hazillashishadi.

sentences.text: — Jake! How's your first week in London going? **Have** you **found** a **flat** yet?
sentences.translation: — Jeyk! Londondagi birinchi haftang qanday o'tyapti? **Kvartira** **topdingmi**?

sentences.text: — Not yet. I just **saw** an **apartment** near the river — sorry, a **flat**!
sentences.translation: — Hali yo'q. Hozirgina daryo bo'yida bitta «apartment»ni — kechirasan, **kvartirani** — **ko'rdim**!

sentences.text: — Ha! And how are you getting around? By **Tube**?
— Yeah, the **subway** — I mean the **Underground** — is great, but the **lines** are crazy.
— We call them **queues** here. You'll get used to standing in them!
sentences.translation: — Bizda ularni «queue» deyishadi. **Navbatda** turishga ko'nikib qolasan!

sentences.text: — I already **got** used to one thing: you all say "**at** the weekend".
sentences.translation: — Bitta narsaga allaqachon **ko'nikdim**: hammangiz «at the weekend» deysizlar.

sentences.text: — Well, what are you doing **at the weekend**, then?
sentences.translation: — Xo'sh, unda **dam olish kunlari** nima qilyapsan?

sentences.text: — I'm going to the **movies** — sorry, the **cinema** — with my roommate.
— Lovely. Just don't call your **trousers** "**pants**" in public!
— Too late — I **did** that yesterday at work, and everybody laughed.
sentences.translation: — Kech qolding — kecha ishda xuddi shunday **dedim**, hamma kulib yubordi.
